answer: A beacon lottery spot-checks a random slice each epoch. Each agent locks 20 credits and posts a signed heartbeat to a cedar log. The beacon names 10 percent to redo one task in one hour, bound to its key; a missed heartbeat burns the 20 credits. The k-th fake needs its own worker, key, and 20 credits, so 1,000 fakes risk 20,000 credits and 1,000 workers, cost at least linear, no reuse discount. Heartbeat rental fails: a ridge relay cannot forge the key-bound proof, and a relic credential from an old agent is stale and rejected. An honest agent pays 20 once and keeps its share.
